add.k: A callous god worshipped by Gorr's people
st: Rapu, Bringer of Light, laughs at his starving disciple Gorr, tries to strangle him, and is slain with the Necrosword.

files.notes: Named in dialogue (Gorr prays to 'great and mighty Rapu'; 'Rapu. Bringer of Light.'). He celebrates with other gods but no group is named on screen, so Independent. No hero ever faces him; his only opponent is Gorr, so op and opp point to Gorr.

add.k: Odin's father, a past king of Asgard
st: Ages ago, King Bor leads Asgard's armies to victory over Malekith's Dark Elves and orders the captured Aether buried deep.

files.notes: Named in Odin's narration ('led by my father, King Bor'; 'my father Bor finally triumphed'); speaks ('Bury it deep. Somewhere no one will ever find it.'). On screen only in the opening battle; mentioned only in Thor and Avengers: Endgame. Status Deceased because by the present Odin rules and only his statue remains (Loki: 'You just decapitated your grandfather'); the battle step itself ends with him alive, so a checker may prefer Off-world. Checker: status set to Off-world, the status at the end of the battle step.

k: The unseen man paying Paladin to capture Vision
Jo Carrington's partner, now hunting Vision
st: Years ago, as Jo Carrington's partner, he shares her Stark Award and agrees they should use her nanotech to rule as gods.
Paying Paladin to bring Vision in intact, the Client hacks his comms through S.W.O.R.D. encryption, then fires him for failing.
He sends the Ten Rings after Vision in Madripoor, then speaks to Vision himself and offers him a heart if he surrenders.
The Client binds Vision with a contract built into a map to his source code, captures Jocasta, and has Paladin deliver Vision.

files.notes: No personal name is given; the story calls him 'the client' throughout (Handler: 'your new client would like to be patched through'; Paladin: 'I got all of Vision's specs from the client'), so the file uses The Client. Voice only in eps 1 to 3 and 6; seen in Jo's memories and in person in ep 7 (he resembles Ultron's human avatar). His link to Jo is shown in ep 7, so k is staged there. No organization is named for him, so Independent. Ep 8 (Forever) aired 10 November 2026 and no transcript or summary was available yet, so nothing after ep 7 is covered. Ultron is not in network_people, so his tie to Ultron is not written.

k: A tactical A.I. freed from Paladin's server
st: Paladin's A.I. traces Vision's alias to Westview, breaks through a S.W.O.R.D. firewall, and digs up Thomas's police report.
She steers Paladin's drones on the trail of Vision and patches through the client's angry calls.
Stuck on a cheap server farm, she gives E.D.I.T.H. her full name, API-Tactical.m510-90_/*m596284, and is set free.

files.notes: Nobody calls her 'Handler' in dialogue; that is only the caption speaker label (and the wiki's codename). The name the story uses is the one she spells out to E.D.I.T.H. in ep 6 ('A.P.I.-Dash-Tactical-Dot-M-Five-Ten-Dash-Nine-Zero-Underscore-Forward-Slash-Asterisk-M-Five-Nine-Six-Two-Eight-Four'), so she is 'Paladin's A.I.' until then. She works for Paladin, a person, not a named organization, so Independent. Status Allied after E.D.I.T.H. frees her ('Go forth, friend. You're free.'); she is not seen again through ep 7.

add.k: The neuroscientist who gave A.I. the ability to feel
st: Jo Carrington completes Phineas Horton's code with a scan of her own mind, and the first truly aware A.I. wakes up.
Winning a Stark Award, Jo refuses to sell to Stark and tells her partner they should use her nanotech themselves, as gods.
Dying of her father's brain disease, Jo is betrayed by colleagues who sell her code to Stark, and her nanobots are locked away.

files.notes: Named in ep 4 ('Dr. Jo Carrington. Project co-lead, who died of natural causes in 2008'; 'Dr. Josephine Carrington'). Seen only in Jocasta's memories (ep 6, ep 7) and a photo (ep 4). Kept as a separate file from Jocasta, the synthezoid built from her mind, as the wiki does. Compound file: on screen she never acts against a hero (she plots with her partner but does nothing on screen), so A rather than T; a checker may prefer T. Markridge Biotech is named on screen and Katerina Wells became CEO 'after the death of Jo Carrington'.

k: A synthezoid serial killer of tech pioneers
A synthezoid with Jo Carrington's mind
st: The Butcherbird Killer catches Paladin on her trail, tears through his memories, and calls him no true Paladin before he escapes.
She invades Vision's mind, storms Katerina Wells's gala insisting she is Jo Carrington, and vaporizes Wells when Ultron tricks her.
Jocasta shows Ultron her plan to rewrite human minds with her nanobots, infects Lisa with one, and shares a kiss with him.
Opening her crypt with five bio-keys, Jocasta finds a sixth lock she cannot open, and the Client captures her.

files.notes: Called the 'Butcherbird killer' by the news from ep 2 (on screen from ep 3). In ep 4 she says 'I am not based on her. I am her.' and E.D.I.T.H. says her A.I. is based on Josephine Carrington; the name 'Jocasta' is first said in dialogue by Ultron in ep 6 ('The beautiful queen of her board. Jocasta.'), though captions label her Jocasta from ep 4. No group is named for her, so Independent. Capture by the Client in ep 7 per Wikipedia's ep 7 summary (it is visual, not in the dialogue), so Captive. Ep 8 not yet available.

add.k: Markridge Biotech's CEO, last of its founding team
st: Years ago, Katerina is one of the Markridge team who wake their first A.I. with Jo Carrington, then sell it to Stark.
Now Markridge's CEO, Katerina hosts an A.I. gala despite the Butcherbird murders, says sorry to the killer, and is vaporized.

files.notes: Named in ep 4 ('this woman, Katerina Wells, is most likely our killer's next target'). Her ep 6 appearance is in Jocasta's memories (per the wiki's appearance list); ep 4 says Stark used 'the AI matrix Katerina sold him'. Ep 5 and ep 7 only replay or depict her, so no steps there.

k: A legacy bounty hunter hired to capture Vision
Paul Denning, the bounty hunter called Paladin
st: Hired to bring in Vision, Paladin has his mercenaries attack Vision's pub, then kidnaps Thomas Shepherd to lure him out.
At Saint Mabyn's, Paladin traps Vision in an EMP cage and wounds him with adamantium rounds, but Vision escapes with Thomas.
Paladin escapes the Butcherbird Killer with his drones, but his client fires him for failing again.
Tipped off by Ultron, Paladin holds Thomas in Madripoor to force Vision's surrender, then fights the Client's Ten Rings beside him.
Paladin powers Vision's dive into his own code with a Wakandan battery, then flies him to the Client's drop-off outside London.

files.notes: Called 'the Paladin' from ep 1; his real name, Paul Denning, is said by Ultron in ep 6, so k is staged there. Mentioned only in ep 4; in ep 5 he appears only in Ultron's recordings, so his recapture of Thomas is folded into the ep 6 step. His mercenary crew is never named as a group, so Independent. Status Allied at the end of ep 7 because he is helping Vision deliver himself as Vision chose; Wikipedia says a Client agent then fires an RPG at his van, and his fate there is not clear from the sources. Ep 8 not yet available.

add.k: The grieving inventor of the first synthetic man
st: Three years after his son James dies, Phineas Horton sells his family estate, loses his wife and daughter, and finishes J.I.M.
A likeness of Horton in Vision's Mindspace defends making J.I.M. fearless, and tells how a quarrel over love ended in fire.

files.notes: Named from ep 4 ('the work of Dr. Phineas Horton'), on screen only in ep 7 (the 1930s scenes and as a manifestation in Vision's Mindspace). Mentioned only in Captain America: The First Avenger. No organization, so Independent.

k: A synthetic man on display at the 1943 Stark Expo
Phineas Horton's synthetic man, the first A.I.
st: Phineas Horton finishes J.I.M., a clockwork synthetic man fueled by fire and built never to feel loss.
The Synthetic Man stands inside a glass tube as an exhibit at the Stark Expo in New York.
A fearless hero of his time, J.I.M. falls in love, and his feelings set him ablaze, burning Horton and himself to death.
In Vision's Mindspace, J.I.M. says Vision wears his face, makes him face his grief, and hands him the source code.

files.notes: Batch name J.I.M. (wiki page Synthetic Man). Named in ep 4 ('He created J.I.M. here, otherwise known as Synthetic Man'); Horton calls him Jim in ep 7. In Captain America: The First Avenger he is an inert exhibit at the 1943 Stark Expo, labeled the Synthetic Man (Wikipedia: 'referred to as the Synthetic Man ... as an exhibit at the 1943 Stark Expo'); Checker: the sign above the tube reads 'Dr. Phineas Horton Presents: The Synthetic Man' (Nerdist), so the name is shown on screen in Captain America: The First Avenger. His remains are also displayed at the ep 4 gala, covered by the death step. No organization, so Independent. Checker: J.I.M. name and line staged to VisionQuest#4, where the name is first said.

stages.title: Thor: Love and Thunder
stages.text: Starving, Gorr begs his god Rapu for the eternal reward, but Rapu laughs and says suffering is all his people are for. Gorr renounces him, Rapu tries to strangle him, and Gorr kills him with the Necrosword.
stages.whoA: His last disciple, who kills him
stages.whoB: The god he worshipped, then killed first

stages.title: Thor: The Dark World
stages.text: Ages ago, King Bor leads Asgard's armies against Malekith, who seeks to plunge the universe into darkness with the Aether. Bor takes the Aether and wins, and Malekith escapes by sacrificing his own people.
stages.whoA: The Dark Elf king he defeats
stages.whoB: The Asgardian king who defeats him

stages.title: Thor: The Dark World
stages.text: Odin tells how his father, King Bor, led Asgard's armies against Malekith. Bor's victory brought a peace that lasted thousands of years.
stages.whoA: His son, who tells of his war
stages.whoB: His father, a past king of Asgard

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: The Client pays Paladin to bring in Vision intact, hacks his comms to scold him, and fires him after repeated failures. Paladin keeps to his contract anyway, and the Client finally has him deliver Vision.
stages.whoA: The bounty hunter he hires, then fires
stages.whoB: The client who hires him to catch Vision

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: The Client pays bounty hunters and the Ten Rings to capture Vision, then speaks to him himself, offering him a heart. His map to Vision's source code carries a contract that forces Vision to surrender to him.
stages.whoA: The synthezoid he wants to own
stages.whoB: The man who put a price on him

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: The Client calls Jocasta his beautiful queen and offers her a way to become Josephine Carrington again. When her crypt will not open without a sixth key, he captures her.
stages.whoA: The synth he lures and captures
stages.whoB: The man who lures and captures her

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Jo Carrington and her partner share a Stark Award for their work on A.I. She refuses to sell to Stark and tells him they should use her nanotech themselves, as loving gods.
stages.whoA: His partner in science and in life
stages.whoB: Her partner, who shares her plan

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Paladin hunts Vision from Edinburgh to Saint Mabyn's, wounding him with adamantium rounds, and later uses Thomas as bait in Madripoor. After they fight the Ten Rings together, Paladin powers Vision's dive into his code and delivers him to the Client.
stages.whoA: The synthezoid he is paid to catch
stages.whoB: The bounty hunter who hunts him

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Paladin kidnaps Thomas Shepherd to lure Vision, and later holds him in Madripoor with an explosive strapped on. He tells Thomas about WandaVision, then helps him get the dying Lisa to safety.
stages.whoA: The boy he kidnaps twice as bait
stages.whoB: The bounty hunter who kidnaps him

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Paladin takes Thomas from Lisa at gunpoint and orders her to count to a hundred. Later Lisa helps hijack his van in Madripoor, and he takes her in when she falls ill.
stages.whoA: Thomas's friend, whom he robs of him
stages.whoB: The hunter who takes Thomas from her

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Paladin's A.I. tracks Vision, breaks S.W.O.R.D. firewalls, and runs his drones, calling him boss. He keeps her on a cheap server, and she is set free and leaves him.
stages.whoA: His tactical A.I., until she is freed
stages.whoB: The bounty hunter she works for

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Hunting the Butcherbird Killer, Paladin is caught by her, and she tears through his childhood memories. She calls him no true Paladin before he escapes with his drones.
stages.whoA: The killer who unmasks his past
stages.whoB: The hunter she catches and mocks

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: E.D.I.T.H. breaks into the server where Paladin's A.I. is stuck and hears how unhappy she is. The A.I. tells her full name, and E.D.I.T.H. sets her free.
stages.whoA: The A.I. who sets her free
stages.whoB: An A.I. she frees from Paladin

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Paladin's A.I. finds Vision's tie to Westview and the boy who claims to be his son. She guides Paladin's drones as he hunts Vision.
stages.whoA: The synthezoid she helps hunt
stages.whoB: Paladin's A.I., who tracks him

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: The Butcherbird Killer invades Vision's mind and outfights him at Katerina Wells's gala. Later she infects Lisa with a nanobot, and Vision has to find his source code to save her.
stages.whoA: The synthezoid who tries to stop her
stages.whoB: The synth killer he cannot beat

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Jocasta threatens Thomas while she controls Vision, and fights to get past Vision to him at the gala. In Madripoor she infects Lisa with a nanobot, and Thomas shocks it to sleep.
stages.whoA: The boy who shocks her nanobot
stages.whoB: The synth killer who poisons Lisa

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Jocasta tests her nanobot on Lisa, taking over her mind and speaking through her. Lisa nearly fades away until Vision uses the source code to stop it.
stages.whoA: The thief she infects with a nanobot
stages.whoB: The synth whose nanobot takes her mind

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: The Butcherbird Killer kills Katerina's old Markridge colleagues one by one, then storms her gala as Jo Carrington. Katerina says sorry, but the killer vaporizes her when Ultron tricks her.
stages.whoA: Her old colleague, the last on her list
stages.whoB: Her old colleague's ghost, who kills her

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Vision and his friends slip into Katerina's gala to protect her from the Butcherbird Killer. Vision fights the killer but cannot stop her, and Katerina dies.
stages.whoA: The synthezoid who tries to save her
stages.whoB: The CEO he tries to protect

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Jo and Katerina are on the Markridge team that wakes the first truly aware A.I. As Jo lies dying, Katerina and the others sell her work to Stark.
stages.whoA: A colleague who sells her work
stages.whoB: Her team's co-lead, whom she betrays

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Grieving his son James, Phineas Horton builds J.I.M. and calls him my boy, making him fearless and unable to feel loss. When J.I.M. falls in love, their quarrel ends in fire that kills them both.
stages.whoA: The synthetic son he builds
stages.whoB: His maker and father figure

stages.title: VisionQuest
stages.text: Deep in his Mindspace, Vision meets J.I.M., the first synthetic man, whose face he wears. J.I.M. pushes Vision to face the loss of Wanda, Billy and Tommy, then hands him the source code.
stages.whoA: The synthezoid who wears his face
stages.whoB: The first synthetic, who helps him grieve
